tagline: Europe's leading airport operator managing major transport hubs across Spain and international destinations
hero_kpi_rationale: Revenue represents Aena's primary operational metric, reflecting airport activity levels across its network. The 1,238 million euros for H1 2020 captures the significant pandemic-driven decline in passenger traffic and airport services.
company_description: Aena S.M.E., S.A., together with its subsidiaries, engages in the management of airports in Spain, Brazil, the United Kingdom, Mexico, and Colombia. The company operates through Airports, Real Estate Services, Región de Murcia International Airport, and International segments. It also manages commercial spaces in airport terminals, and a network of car parks; and leasing or transfer use of land, office buildings, warehouses, hangars, and cargo vessels to airlines, air cargo operators, handling agents and other airport service providers. In addition, the company is involved in the operation of duty-free shops, food and beverage, and specialty shops; rental of cars; advertising; baggage wrapping machines; other vending machines; regulated services, including pharmacies, tobacconists, lottery vendors, etc.; and provision of financial services, such as currency exchange, VAT refunds, and ATMs, as well as advisory services to international airports. Aena S.M.E., S.A. was formerly known as Aena, S.A. and changed its name to Aena S.M.E., S.A. in April 2017. The company was founded in 1991 and is headquartered in Madrid, Spain. Aena S.M.E., S.A. operates as a subsidiary of Entidad Pública

risks.title: Airport tariff regulation (DORA)
risks.summary: Aena is subject to airport tariff regulation through DORA (Regulatory Orientation Document), which determines the charges collected. Any future changes could limit its growth or require costly investments.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is mentioned first in the operational section, with strong language ("applicable regulation", "limits on activities"), stable trend, and represents a core issue for Aena's business model.

risks.title: Impact of Brexit on air traffic
risks.summary: The UK's exit from the EU (Brexit), effective January 2020, creates regulatory and operational uncertainty. A no-deal departure could have reduced air links and passenger traffic to UK airports.
risks.score_rationale: Brexit is explicitly identified as a major operational risk, with concerned language ("uncertain outcome", "no deal"), stable trend, and directly affects passenger flows.

risks.title: Dependence on passenger traffic
risks.summary: Aena's revenues are highly dependent on passenger volume and flight operations. Any decline in traffic (crisis, pandemic, competition) directly impacts its operational and financial performance.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is central in the document, with strong language ("directly linked", "traffic levels"), stable trend, and fundamental to Aena's revenue.

risks.title: Cybersecurity risks
risks.summary: As a critical infrastructure operator, Aena is exposed to cyberattacks that could disrupt airport management systems, compromise passenger data, or interrupt operations.
risks.score_rationale: Although not detailed here, cyber risk is implicit in modern operational threats to critical infrastructure. Regulatory language and sector nature justify high severity, upward trend.

risks.title: Increased competition among European airports
risks.summary: European airports compete fiercely to attract airlines and international routes. Aena must continuously improve its offering to maintain its traffic share against hubs such as Frankfurt or Amsterdam.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is implied by sensitivity to traffic and airline decisions. Language on operational and regulatory conditions indicates competitive pressure, upward trend.

risks.title: Regulation on security and environment
risks.summary: Aena must comply with strict regulations on personal and property security and environmental protection. Future changes could require significant investments or restrict operational capacity.
risks.score_rationale: The text explicitly mentions regulatory developments on security and environment. Constraining language ("could limit", "significant expenses"), stable trend.
